title: TEMPO (Tracking, Engagement, Messaging & Participant Outreach): automated survey scheduling and participant messaging for longitudinal studies
description:
TEMPO is a server that automates participant communication and completion tracking for research studies that follow participants for months or years. It supports studies where each participant's schedule depends on their own dates and completed forms. TEMPO sends SMS and email, tracks form completion and progress through study phases, and supports two-way texting through the study's own phone number. The study's survey platform remains the source of truth.

Schedules are declared as rules that refer to fields in the study's survey database. Each rule uses a field to decide whether a message is owed and a date field to determine its timing. For example, a reminder can start fourteen days after a baseline visit and repeat weekly up to three times while a form remains incomplete. Each run reads current data from REDCap or Qualtrics, rebuilds the schedule, checks completion and previous sends, then sends eligible messages and records them. Completing a form stops its reminders.

The repository holds source files only, including a synthetic example schedule, with no participant data or credentials. Study identifiers are replaced with placeholders, and dashboard screenshots use synthetic records. It is a record of a system running participant communication for NIH-funded longitudinal research involving several hundred participants. It is not installable software, and there is no quickstart.
